title: Beheading Video of Oyo Teacher Sparks National Outrage; Tinubu Condemns 'Barbaric' Act
detail: A video released by kidnappers on May 17 showed the beheading of Michael Oyedokun, a teacher at Community High School in Ahoro-Esinele, Oriire LGA, Oyo State, who had been abducted along with 45 others (including 39 students) in the May 15 attack. The video ignited nationwide outrage, with President Tinubu personally condemning the act as 'barbaric' and pledging to 'work to arrest the killers.' House Speaker Tajudeen Abbas called for the swift rescue of all remaining captives. Civil society organizations, celebrities, and labor unions joined in demanding immediate government action. The Oyo State government offered a ₦20 million reward for information leading to the rescue of the captives. Military officials confirmed Tucano A-29 Super Tucano surveillance jets were being deployed over forest areas where hostages were believed to be held. The murder echoed the 2014 Chibok kidnapping crisis and intensified calls for federal military action in Oyo State's porous borders with Kwara and Kogi.

media.caption: National outrage follows beheading of Oyo teacher abducted in school attack

title: Nigerian Senate Condemns Wave of School Abductions as 'Attack on Nigeria's Future'
detail: The Nigerian Senate passed a formal resolution on May 17 condemning the mass school abductions in Borno and Oyo states, declaring them 'an attack on Nigeria's future.' Senators called on the Tinubu administration to mobilize all military assets for the immediate rescue of captives and demanded comprehensive security protocols be established for schools nationwide. Senate President Godswill Akpabio presided over the extraordinary session. The resolution also called for an emergency briefing from the Minister of Defence and the National Security Adviser on the security situation in the northeast and southwest. Civil society groups simultaneously demanded that the government address the structural failure to protect students — drawing comparisons to the 2014 Chibok crisis that galvanized the global #BringBackOurGirls movement.

media.caption: Nigerian Senate condemns school abductions, demands military rescue of hostages
